app.nexbeat: Find music and request it from Lidarr or nexcrate without using their interface.
app.nexcrate: A replacement for Radarr, Sonarr and Lidarr: movies, series and music in one place, several versions per title.
app.nexdeck: Every service in the house on one surface: look, check, step in.
app.nexmail: Mail, calendar, contacts and tasks, self-hosted and gathered in one window.
app.nexpulse: Speed tests on a schedule, with a history you can still read later.
app.nexview: Requests for your media server, plus the tools an operator needs afterwards.

about.appsIntro: From the same workshop, all open source and built for your own network. Each runs on its own, none needs the other.
about.tagline: Connection manager in the browser for SSH and SFTP. Part of the nex apps.
about.title: About
about.upToDate: You are up to date. Checked {{when}}.

account.lead: Name, role and how you sign in.
account.linkLead: Link your account to your identity at {{provider}}. Afterwards you can sign in there; your password here stays valid and still opens the vault.
account.linked: Linked. You can sign in through {{provider}}.
account.linkedNow: Linked. From now on signing in through the provider works too.
account.oidcOnly: This account signs in only through {{provider}} and has no password here. Change the vault password under Vault.
account.passwordLead: It is your vault password too; the vault is sealed again with the new password. Other browsers have to sign in again.
account.title: Your account
account.linkPasswordLead: Your password once more, to be safe. Then you go to {{provider}}; on the way back the account is linked to the identity that is signed in there.
account.signOutEverywhereHint: Ends every other browser and terminal of this account, right now. This browser stays signed in.

auth.inviteInvalid: This invitation is not valid any more. Ask for a new one.
auth.inviteLead: You get an account as {{role}}. Choose a name and a password.
auth.name: Name
auth.nameHint: Lower-case letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore.
auth.passwordHint: At least {{min}} characters. It also opens your vault.
auth.setupLead: Create the operator account. It manages accounts, sharing and settings.
auth.title: Sign in
auth.vaultNote: Your vault is encrypted with this password too. If you forget it, nobody gets to the keys and passwords in it any more, not even the operator.

backups.createSub: Takes a few seconds. Open sessions keep running.
backups.deleteWarning: Gone is gone. If you might still need this state, download it first.
backups.downloadWhat: You get an encrypted ZIP with the database and the key secret.key. It holds accounts, connections, sharing, stored host keys, the settings and every vault. The vaults stay encrypted inside the archive just as they are: only the password of the respective account opens them, not the password of the archive.
backups.folderHint: The files live in {{folder}}. They cannot be reached through the web server, only through this button and the file system. Accounts, connections and host keys are stored there unencrypted, the vaults stay encrypted there too. Whoever can read the folder sees who connects where, but no keys and no passwords.
backups.intro: nextrmnl makes a copy by itself before every schema change and on a schedule. That copy lives in the same folder as the database, though: if the volume is lost, it is gone with it. It only becomes a backup once you download it and keep it somewhere else.
backups.keepHint: Only automatic copies are limited, ones made by hand stay. One copy costs a few MiB.
backups.noteHint: What is this backup for? “Before moving to the new server” helps you more in three months than a date.
backups.passwordTooShort: At least {{min}} characters. The archive holds the access to all your machines.
backups.passwordWarning: Remember this password. There is no second key and no way back: without the password the file is worthless. The archive opens with 7-Zip or WinRAR, so you do not depend on nextrmnl.
backups.title: Backups

clipboard.confirmLead: Each line runs as if you had typed it and pressed Enter.
clipboard.denied: The browser blocked the clipboard. Ctrl+V still works.
clipboard.needsHttps: Pasting with a right click needs HTTPS. Ctrl+V always works.

edit.authAskHint: nextrmnl stores nothing, you type the password when connecting.
edit.authKeyHint: Recommended. Sign-in without a password, the key is stored encrypted in your vault.
edit.authPasswordHint: Stored encrypted in your vault. For devices that cannot use keys.
edit.hostKeyUnknown: Not known yet. nextrmnl shows it on the first connection and asks.
edit.jumpHint: For machines that are only reachable through another one, such as behind a bastion server.
edit.keepaliveHint: Sends a sign of life every 30 seconds so routers and firewalls do not cut the line.
edit.name: Name
edit.noKeys: There is no key in your vault yet. Generate one under Vault, or choose another sign-in method.
edit.nobodyToShare: There are no other accounts yet.
edit.ownUserHint: {{owner}} connects as {{user}}. Leave empty to use the same name.
edit.passwordHint: Leave empty to keep the stored one.
edit.shareLead: Which accounts should see this connection in their list?
edit.shareNote: Shared are name, address and settings. Your keys and passwords stay in your vault: whoever connects signs in with their own access.
edit.sharedOwnAccess: Your own access to this connection: user, method and key come from your vault. {{owner}} sees none of it.
edit.sharedReadOnly: {{owner}} shared this connection with you. Host, port and settings are read-only; under Sign-in you set your own access.
edit.startCommandHint: Optional. Runs right after sign-in, for example to start tmux.
edit.ownStartCommandHint: Your own command on this shared connection. The owner's command never runs in your shell.
edit.vaultNote: You manage keys and passwords under Vault.

empty.lead: Pick a connection from the list or connect directly.
empty.quickError: That is not an address. Example: admin@192.0.2.40 or admin@nas:2222
empty.quickHint: Like in PuTTY: user@host, the port after a colon. Without a user, root is used.
empty.title: No session open

byCode.account_locked: Too many failed sign-ins. This account now waits a quarter of an hour.
byCode.archive_invalid: This is not a nextrmnl backup archive, or the password is wrong.
byCode.backup_newer: This backup comes from a newer version. Update nextrmnl first.
byCode.backup_not_found: This backup does not exist any more.
byCode.cannot_delete_self: You cannot delete your own account.
byCode.cannot_demote_self: You cannot take the operator role from yourself.
byCode.file_invalid: This is not a nextrmnl vault file.
byCode.invalid_host: That is not a host name or address.
byCode.invalid_input: Part of the input is not valid.
byCode.invalid_key: This is not a private key nextrmnl can read.
byCode.invalid_name: A name has 2 to 64 characters: lower-case letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore.
byCode.invalid_targets: These entries are neither networks nor names: {{entries}}
byCode.invalid_targets_mode: Unknown choice for the allowed targets.
byCode.invite_invalid: This invitation is not valid any more.
byCode.issuer_invalid: No OpenID Connect provider answers at this address.
byCode.issuer_unreachable: The provider could not be reached at this address.
byCode.jump_self: A connection cannot jump through itself.
byCode.key_name_taken: A key with this name exists already.
byCode.key_not_found: This key is not in your vault.
byCode.key_required: Choose a key from the vault.
byCode.log_level_from_environment: The log level is fixed by NEXTRMNL_LOG_LEVEL and cannot be changed here.
byCode.missing_header: This request was blocked because it did not come from the nextrmnl interface.
byCode.network: nextrmnl cannot be reached. Is it running?
byCode.not_found: That does not exist any more.
byCode.not_signed_in: You are signed out. Sign in again.
byCode.oidc_account: This account signs in through OIDC and has no password here.
byCode.oidc_denied: The provider refused the sign-in or you cancelled it.
byCode.oidc_email_taken: This email address already belongs to an account linked to a different provider account.
byCode.oidc_email_unverified: The provider did not report the email address as verified.
byCode.oidc_exchange_failed: The provider did not accept the sign-in code. Check client ID and secret.
byCode.oidc_link_mismatch: The link does not match the signed-in session. Try again.
byCode.oidc_no_account: There is no account here for this identity. The operator has to invite you or allow new accounts through the provider.
byCode.oidc_only_account: This account has no password and can only sign in through the provider.
byCode.oidc_provider_unreachable: The provider could not be reached.
byCode.oidc_state_mismatch: The sign-in expired or came from another window. Try again.
byCode.oidc_subject_taken: This identity at the provider already belongs to another account.
byCode.oidc_token_invalid: The provider's token did not pass verification.
byCode.operator_only: Only the operator may do this.
byCode.passphrase_needed: This key is protected. Enter its passphrase so nextrmnl can read it.
byCode.password_account: For password accounts the password is the vault password too.
byCode.password_login_off: Sign-in with a password is turned off.
byCode.public_url_invalid: The public address needs http:// or https:// and a host name, without a path.
byCode.session_not_found: This session does not exist any more.
byCode.sftp_failed: The file transfer failed. Is SFTP enabled on the machine? On a Synology: Control Panel, File Services, FTP, enable the SFTP service.
byCode.signed_out: The sign-in behind this terminal has ended: signed out, reset, or ended by the operator.
byCode.too_many_attempts: Too many refused sign-ins at targets in a row. Wait a moment and try again.
byCode.target_not_allowed: This target is outside the allowed networks. The operator can widen them under Security.
byCode.unknown_account: One of the accounts does not exist.
byCode.unknown_version: This backup lacks the version it came from.
byCode.vault_exists: This account already has a vault.
byCode.vault_locked: The vault is locked. Enter your password to open it.
byCode.vault_not_set_up: This account has no vault yet.
byCode.second_factor_expired: The second step timed out or went wrong too often. Start again with your password.
byCode.second_factor_setup_required: The operator requires a second factor. Set it up under Account.
byCode.totp_code_wrong: The code is not right. Check the time on your phone and try again.
byCode.totp_enabled: The second factor is already on. Turn it off first.
byCode.totp_enrolment_expired: The enrolment timed out. Start again.
byCode.totp_not_enabled: The second factor is not on.
byCode.use_disable: You turn your own second factor off under Account, with your password.

errors.http: The server answered with an error (HTTP {{status}}).
errors.internal: Something went wrong on the server. Request: {{id}}
errors.network: nextrmnl cannot be reached. Is it running?
errors.tooManyAttemptsMinutes_one: Too many attempts. Try again in {{count}} minute.
errors.tooManyAttemptsMinutes_other: Too many attempts. Try again in {{count}} minutes.
errors.tooManyAttemptsSeconds_one: Too many attempts. Try again in {{count}} second.
errors.tooManyAttemptsSeconds_other: Too many attempts. Try again in {{count}} seconds.

files.deleteDirText: {{name}} is deleted on the machine with everything inside it. This cannot be undone.
files.deleteText: {{name}} is deleted on the machine. This cannot be undone.
files.name: Name
files.title: Files

hostkey.changedHint: If you reinstalled the machine, this is expected. Otherwise: do not connect and check first.
hostkey.changedLead: {{where}} presents a different key than last time. That happens after a reinstall, but it can also mean someone is intercepting the connection.
hostkey.howToCheck: On the machine itself, this shows it:
hostkey.newLead: nextrmnl has never talked to {{where}}. Compare the fingerprint before you trust the machine. After that nextrmnl will not ask again unless the key changes.

list.collapse: Collapse the list, it then floats above the terminal
list.empty: No connection yet. Create the first one with the plus.
list.removeText: The connection disappears from your list and from the lists of every account it was shared with. A stored password for it is deleted too.
list.title: Connections

logs.alwaysLead: What is in it: start, end, account, target and result of every session, sign-ins, host key decisions, sharing, backups. For SFTP the path and the size, never the content.
logs.confirmClear: All entries so far are deleted. New messages are still recorded.
logs.intro: The application log. Messages are in English because they help when searching the web for an error.
logs.levelHint: A filter always includes the higher levels: “WARNING” also shows the errors. Clicking a request number shows only that request.

modeDesc.detailed: Plus the way there: every step of the connection setup, the host key check, SFTP operations with path and size.
modeDesc.normal: What happened: sessions, sign-ins, backups, plus warnings and errors.
modeDesc.trace: Plus the raw data of the SSH library: negotiation, channels, window sizes. Very many lines, but still never terminal content.

logs.modeEnv: Fixed by the environment variable NEXTRMNL_LOG_LEVEL and not changeable here.
logs.modeIntro: Logging is always on, the level only decides how much. “Normal” is enough day to day; turn on more for a while to track down a problem.
logs.modeUntil: Switches back to “Normal” by itself at {{time}}.

never.files: Contents of files transferred over SFTP, and clipboard contents.
never.secrets: Passwords, passphrases, private keys, tokens and session identifiers, not even in error messages.
never.terminal: What is shown or typed in the terminal. No commands, no output, no keystrokes.

logs.neverLead: At no level, not even at “Everything”:
logs.neverTitle: What is never in the log
logs.retention: The log rolls over at 5 MiB (25 MiB at the deep levels), 3 older files are kept and everything is deleted after 14 days. The download includes the older files.
logs.title: Log
logs.traceWarning: Only turn on “Everything” when someone explicitly asks for it: this level records every line of the SSH library.

password.label: Password
password.rememberHint: Then nextrmnl will not ask next time.
password.storedFailed: The stored password was refused. Enter the current one; with the switch it replaces the stored one.
password.title: Password for {{target}}

restore.envKey: Careful: NEXTRMNL_SECRET_KEY is set as an environment variable. Then the variable wins and the key from the archive is ignored. If its value differs from the one in the backup, the OIDC secret and the sign-ins can no longer be read afterwards. The vaults do not depend on it; they still open with the account's password.
restore.intro: Replaces the running installation with the state from a backup. Everything that happened since is lost, including in the vaults of all accounts. nextrmnl makes a backup of the current state first.
restore.noKey: There is no key in this archive, and this installation has none either. Restoring creates a new one, and afterwards the OIDC secret and the sign-ins can no longer be read. Set NEXTRMNL_SECRET_KEY to the value that installation used before you continue.
restore.passwordHint: The password set when the archive was downloaded.
restore.restarting: nextrmnl shuts down and starts again with the backup. As soon as it answers again the page reloads and you land on the sign-in.
restore.sessionsWarning: All open sessions are cut, everyone who is signed in is thrown out, you too. nextrmnl shuts down and starts again with the backup; Docker brings it back, that takes under a minute.
restore.title: Restore a backup
restore.tooNew: This backup comes from version {{version}} and is therefore newer than the running one. nextrmnl can only move data forward, not back. Update nextrmnl first.
restore.unknownVersion: This backup lacks the version it came from. Without it there is no telling whether it fits.
restore.vaultsLink: Go to the vault page to save your own vault as a file first
restore.vaultsWarning: Every vault goes back to the state of this backup. Whatever an account changed in its vault since then is gone afterwards, and as operator you cannot get in to rescue it. Every account can save its vault as a file beforehand and restore it afterwards.

security.allowListHint: Networks and names, separated by commas.
security.otherNote: After ten failed sign-ins in a row nextrmnl waits a quarter of an hour. This cannot be turned off.
security.targetsAllHint: Including any machine on the internet.
security.targetsAllWarn: Anyone with an account can then reach any machine on the internet from your network. Only choose this if you trust every account.
security.targetsLead: Where nextrmnl may open connections. This applies to all accounts and is the boundary to the outside.
security.targetsListHint: Private addresses plus the networks and names you enter.
security.updateCheckHint: Only the request itself is sent: no connections, no accounts, nothing from the vaults. Off by default.
security.updatesLead: nextrmnl can check GitHub once a day for a newer version. The result then shows in the footer and under About.

sessions.keepNote: The history records who connected where and when, not what was typed. It is kept for 90 days.
sessions.lead: Who is connected right now and who was. As operator you see all accounts, a member only themselves.
sessions.title: Sessions

settings.accountsLead: Who may use nextrmnl. Every account has its own connections and its own vault.
settings.clipboardHttps: Pasting with a right click reads the clipboard. The browser only allows that over HTTPS and asks the first time. Ctrl+V works without HTTPS too.
settings.clipboardLead: Like in PuTTY and Windows Terminal.
settings.confirmMultilineHint: When pasting several lines nextrmnl first shows what will arrive, because many shells run each line at once. A single line arrives without a line break and does not run by itself.
settings.copyOnSelectHint: Like in PuTTY: whatever you select is in the clipboard at once.
settings.deleteAccountText: The account disappears with its connections, its sharing and its vault. The vault was readable only with this account's password anyway.
settings.inviteLead: You get a link that is valid for seven days. Whoever opens it chooses name and password themselves.
settings.inviteLinkLead: Pass this link on. It is shown only once and is good for one account.
settings.inviteLinkWarning: Whoever has the link gets an account. Send it only to the person you mean, over a channel you trust.
settings.inviteNameHint: A suggestion, can be changed when accepting.
settings.keysCopyWhich: Select · Ctrl+Shift+C · Ctrl+Insert · Ctrl+C with a selection
settings.keysWordWhich: Double click takes whole IP addresses and paths · triple click the line
settings.forceSignOutText: Ends every browser and terminal of {{name}}, right now. The account stays and can sign in again.
settings.operatorNote: The operator manages accounts and sharing. Even the operator cannot get into other vaults.
settings.previewNote: Applies to new sessions, open ones keep their settings.
settings.rightClickHint: With a selection it copies, without one it pastes. Off: right click opens the browser's normal menu.
settings.terminalLead: Applies to your account, on every device.
settings.title: Settings

signin.authentikLead: nextrmnl creates everything in authentik itself: provider, application, signing key, the mapping for email_verified and the redirect address. For that it needs an API token once.
signin.autoCreate: Create new accounts through the provider
signin.autoCreateHint: Off: only accounts that exist here already come in through the provider, matched by the verified email address or a link made under Account. On: whoever may see the application at the provider gets a member account on first sign-in.
signin.blueprint: Rather without a token: download the blueprint file
signin.doneText: authentik is set up. You no longer need the token, best delete it in authentik right away.
signin.failedText: The setup stopped. Check the message at the red step and try again.
signin.manualLead: Keycloak, Pocket ID, Authelia, Zitadel and all others with OpenID Connect. nextrmnl reads the rest from the issuer address.
signin.passwordLoginHint: Off: only via OIDC. The operator account keeps its password as an emergency exit.
signin.publicUrlHint: The address people use to reach nextrmnl, for example behind the proxy. It goes into invitation links, is the return address at the OIDC provider and counts in the origin check of the WebSockets. Empty means NEXTRMNL_PUBLIC_URL from the environment, otherwise the address of the request.
signin.publicUrlNote: After a change the provider still knows the old return address. With authentik: below under "Set up with authentik", click "Set up" once more with a fresh API token; that updates the existing provider. Otherwise adjust the return address at the provider by hand.
signin.saved: Saved. The sign-in page now shows the button for the provider.

step.filled: Client ID and secret entered in nextrmnl
step.signingKey: Signing key chosen (RS256) so authentik does not sign with the client secret

signin.tokenHint: In authentik under Directory, Tokens and App passwords, intent API. nextrmnl uses it once and does not store it.
signin.vaultNote: Whoever signs in via OIDC sets their own vault password the first time. Without that password the vault stays closed even if the sign-in works.

fail.connection_lost: The connection to the server was lost.
fail.hostkey: Not connected: the host key was not accepted.
fail.internal_error: Something went wrong on the server. The log names the request id.
fail.key_not_found: The key of this connection is no longer in the vault.
fail.key_unreadable: The key could not be read; the passphrase does not fit.
fail.no_answer: No answer to the question, cancelled.
fail.target_not_allowed: This target is outside the allowed networks.
fail.vault_locked: The vault is locked. Open it and reconnect.

twofactor.codeHint: Six digits from your authenticator app.
twofactor.codesLead: Each code replaces the app once, for example when the phone is gone. Write them down or keep them somewhere safe. They are shown only now.
twofactor.disableText: Afterwards the password alone is enough again. Enter it to confirm.
twofactor.lead: A code from an authenticator app on top of the password, for example Aegis, 2FAS or Google Authenticator. Applies to signing in with a password; whoever comes through the provider brings its second factor along.
twofactor.lowCodes: Only a few recovery codes left. Make new ones while you can still get in.
twofactor.newCodesText: The old codes stop working. Enter your password.
twofactor.oidcOnly: This account signs in through {{provider}}; the provider is in charge of the second factor.
twofactor.recoveryHint: One of the codes you saved when setting up. Each works once.
twofactor.requiredBanner: The operator requires a second factor. Set it up here, then you can carry on.
twofactor.requiredHint: Accounts without a second factor only reach their account page after signing in, until they have set it up. This applies to you as well.
twofactor.requiredSwitch: Require a second factor for all password accounts
twofactor.resetText: Afterwards {{name}} signs in with the password alone again and can set the second factor up anew. Only for an account that has lost its app and its codes.
twofactor.setupPasswordHint: Once more, to be safe: only whoever knows the password turns the second factor on or off.
twofactor.setupScan: Scan the code with your authenticator app or type the key in by hand.
twofactor.stepLead: Password accepted. Now the code from the app for {{name}}.
twofactor.title: Second factor
twofactor.useApp: Back to the code from the app
twofactor.useRecovery: Phone not at hand? Use a recovery code

unlock.lead: Enter your password to use keys and passwords again.
unlock.running_one: {{count}} session keeps running in the background.
unlock.running_other: {{count}} sessions keep running in the background.
unlock.title: Vault locked

vault.deleteText: The private key is gone afterwards. On the machines the public part stays in authorized_keys until you remove it there.
vault.deleteUsed_one: {{count}} connection uses this key. It needs another sign-in method afterwards. On the machines the public part stays until you remove it there.
vault.deleteUsed_other: {{count}} connections use this key. They need another sign-in method afterwards. On the machines the public part stays until you remove it there.
vault.forgotText: Then the vault can no longer be opened, not even by the operator. The connections remain; keys and passwords you enter again.
vault.generatedHint: Add it to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the machine. nextrmnl never shows the private part.
vault.generatedLead: This is the public part. Anyone may see it.
vault.importPassphraseHint: Only needed if the key has one.
vault.keysLead: For signing in without a password. nextrmnl never shows the private part.
vault.lead: Keys and passwords for your connections. Only your password opens it.
vault.noKeys: No key yet. Generate one or paste an existing one.
vault.noPasswords: No connection uses a stored password. Set that in the connection under Sign-in.
vault.openHint: Locks after 30 minutes without input. Nobody but you gets in, not even the operator.
vault.passphraseHint: Optional. nextrmnl then asks for it on every connection.
vault.passwordsLead: For devices that cannot use keys, such as some switches.
vault.privateKeyHint: OpenSSH or PEM format. It is then stored encrypted in the vault.
vault.title: Vault

vaultBackup.exportConfirm: For safety, your vault password once more, even though the vault is open right now.
vaultBackup.exportKeep: Keep the file like a private key. It is encrypted, but whoever has it and guesses your password has all your access.
vaultBackup.exportWhat: The file contains your {{keys}} keys and {{passwords}} stored passwords, encrypted with your vault password. Only someone who knows that password can open it, the operator cannot.
vaultBackup.importLead: A file you downloaded here or on another nextrmnl.
vaultBackup.importNote: When restoring, nextrmnl decrypts the file once in memory and stores the entries in your vault, newly encrypted with your password here. The file itself is not kept.
vaultBackup.importPasswordHint: The password of the account that downloaded the file. It can differ from yours here.
vaultBackup.imported: Restored: {{added_keys}} keys and {{added_passwords}} passwords, skipped: {{skipped_keys}} keys and {{skipped_passwords}} passwords.
vaultBackup.lead: Your vault as a file, encrypted with your vault password. For safekeeping, for moving to another nextrmnl, and for the case that the operator restores a server backup: then every vault goes back to the old state, and your file brings yours back.
vaultBackup.modeMergeHint: What is already here stays. From the file comes what is missing; entries with the same name are skipped.
vaultBackup.modeReplaceHint: Everything in the vault right now is replaced by the contents of the file.
vaultBackup.title: Back up vault

vaultSetup.lead: Your account signs in through OIDC. The vault needs its own password that only you know.
vaultSetup.title: Choose a vault password
vaultSetup.warning: If you forget this password, nobody gets to the keys and passwords in the vault any more, not even the operator. Only an empty new vault remains.
